claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can form a fine, alternating lamellar eutectic microstructure containing FCC and B2 phases.
The stated lamellar microstructure can be produced by either casting or spark-plasma sintering.
The Al-Ni-rich phase is the softer phase, while the B2 or FCC phase is the harder phase.
The numerous lamellar phase boundaries are inherently susceptible to differential oxidation.
Simultaneous elevated-temperature wear and corrosive attack promote selective oxidation at lamellar phase boundaries.
Localized oxidation weakens interfacial bonding between the phases.
Interfacial weakening accelerates corrosion through pitting and preferential dissolution.
Interfacial weakening accelerates wear by facilitating spallation and removal of protective oxide scales.
Elevated temperature accelerates defect diffusion at phase interfaces.
Polarization at phase interfaces contributes to enhanced pitting.
Al-Ni-rich phases possess passive or protective surface films that can be attacked by chloride.
Sliding wear mechanically removes oxide from the Al-Ni-rich phase and exposes fresh alloy to localized corrosion.
Repeated oxide removal and renewed corrosion cause interfacial debonding and spallation, coupling and accelerating both degradation modes.
Selective dissolution of Al-Ni-rich regions increases as temperature increases.
Metastable pits form preferentially at grain boundaries or on the B2 phase.
A lamellar eutectic sample will have greater total mass loss than a composition-matched homogenized single-phase sample under simultaneous wear-corrosion.
The lamellar sample will develop deeper wear tracks and less stable friction because of repeated oxide spallation.
The lamellar sample will exhibit a higher localized-corrosion rate than a homogenized single-phase sample.
Removing distinct phase boundaries by homogenization reduces differential oxidation and mechanical removal of protective scales.
An exceptionally stable oxide layer would suppress or invalidate the proposed degradation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is alternatively defined as either a homogenized single-phase sample or the same lamellar alloy tested under corrosion alone. The explanation that the baseline is protected by an absence of phase boundaries applies only to the homogenized sample, not to the corrosion-only lamellar sample.

The proposed test combines a chloride-containing acidic aqueous solution with temperatures of 600–900 °C, including a nominal 800 °C test, while also referring to an oxidizing service atmosphere. These are incompatible or materially different environmental regimes unless pressure, fluid state, and gas/liquid exposure geometry are specified.
